fields.description: Supplier's invoice number. Letters, digits, hyphen and slash only.

constraints.name: min_exclusive
constraints.description: Before August 2024 an invoice belonged in this table only above 2,50,000.

constraints.name: min_exclusive
constraints.description: From August 2024 the threshold dropped to 1,00,000.

fields.description: Total invoice value including tax. This table carries only high-value supplies to unregistered persons, and the threshold changed with the August 2024 period. The comparison is strictly greater than: an invoice exactly at the threshold does not belong here.

Place of supply as 'NN-Name'; only the numeric prefix is retained. This table is inter-state by definition, so the place of supply must differ from the supplier's own state — except for an SEZ supplier, where the reference skips the check.
Proportion of the tax rate that applies. Emitted as a factor (1.00 or 0.65).
Combined tax rate for this line, in percent. One row per rate.
Taxable value at this rate, excluding tax.
Cess payable on this line. A blank cell produces no csamt key in the payload rather than a zero — see the quirk note.
Operator GSTIN. The template accepts 15 characters in this column, but import rejects any value: e-commerce supplies belong in the ECO tables.

rules.description: Reproduces the reference behavior: this section carries no e-commerce operator GSTIN at all, despite the template's column allowing one.
rules.message: E-Commerce GSTIN must be blank in the B2C(Large) section; report supplies through an operator in the ECO tables.

keys.description: One envelope object per place of supply — this section groups by state, not by recipient, because the recipients are unregistered.
Always empty in this section; whether the key is emitted at all is unconfirmed.

Proportion of the tax rate that applies, as a factor. The reference emits this key ONLY when it is 0.65 and discards every other value, so an unscaled row carries no such key at all. Verified against a file captured from the tool.
Integrated tax. Always present — this section is inter-state by definition, so no central/state split can arise.
Cess. Absent entirely when the source cell is blank — see the quirk note.

derivation_notes.gstr1.item_num: Line item number is derived from the rate, not a sequence: num = rt * 100 + 1.
derivation_notes.gstr1.tax_split: Always resolves to inter-state for this section: iamt = round(txval * rt * 0.01 * diff_percent, 2). The shared derivation reaches that outcome because the section has no invoice-type field, and the pos_differs_from_supplier_state constraint guarantees the place of supply is never the supplier's own state.
derivation_notes.gstr1.cess_unguarded: csamt = round(Cess Amount, 2) when the cell has a value, and no key at all when it is blank. Unlike the shared cess derivation, there is no empty-cell guard here, which is what makes the key vanish rather than read 0.

notes.text: The central/state tax branch of the reference's item mapping is unreachable for this section. It is guarded by 'place of supply equals the supplier's state AND the supplier is not an SEZ unit', but a non-SEZ row with a matching state is rejected before it gets there, and an SEZ supplier fails the second half of the guard. Every line therefore carries integrated tax, and camt/samt are deliberately absent from the payload mapping above.

The invoice-value threshold is compared strictly: a value exactly equal to the threshold is rejected, not accepted. The official template's own column validation carries the post-August-2024 minimum of 100000, so a workbook prepared from the current template but filed for an earlier period must still clear the older 250000 bar.

GSTN's shipped sample CSV for this table populates E-Commerce GSTIN on one row, which import rejects, and sets every invoice value to 250000.01 — a value that clears the pre-August-2024 threshold by one paisa but would fail for any period before it if the threshold were compared inclusively. Layout reference only, not a positive fixture.
This section has no recipient GSTIN, receiver name, reverse-charge flag or invoice type: the recipients are unregistered, so the payload groups by place of supply instead of by counterparty.

The internal 'diffval' flag never reaches the upload JSON — the reference deletes it alongside the tax-rate factor. This resolves what was previously an open question. Verified against a file captured from the tool.

A blank Cess Amount yields no csamt key at all. The reference computes cess for this section without the empty-cell guard it uses in the B2B tables, so a blank cell becomes NaN, the working file records it as null, and the upload step's omit-empty drops the key. An explicit 0 in the cell is a real zero and is emitted. This was previously recorded as a deliberate divergence emitting 0; a file captured from the tool showed that was wrong, and that these two tables are the only ones lacking the guard — every other section emits 0 for a blank cell.

This section has no counterparty column, so the reference's invoice lookup matches on the document number ALONE — across the whole sheet, not within one envelope. Its comparison normalises the absent counterparty id to '' on both sides (returnStructure.js:8536), so the guard that would otherwise separate envelopes is always satisfied. The same number under two different envelope keys is therefore one document with contradictory details: the reference reports it in multiItmErrData and drops the row.
